competences: The learner identify parallel sides and perpendicular height.
The learner calculate trapezium areas and an unknown parallel side.
languageCompetence: Reads, pronounces, spells and correctly uses: trapezium, parallel sides, perpendicular height, area.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify parallel sides and perpendicular height.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to calculate trapezium areas and an unknown parallel side.
priorKnowledge: Learners know triangle areas and can solve simple equations.
materials: Trapezium chart labelled with parallel sides and perpendicular height
references: P 6 Primary SIX MTC Notes Docx (ecolebooks Com)
P.6 PRIMARY SIX MTC NOTES.docx TEACHER.AC

steps.content: Learners know triangle areas and can solve simple equations. Starter: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays trapezium chart labelled with parallel sides and perpendicular height, reviews the prior skill, and asks: "Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm." The teacher records learners’ methods and connects them to area of a trapezium.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous skill, read the starter question, and explain which measurements or operations they would use.

source.quote: Find the area of the trapezium below

steps.content: Area of a trapezium: A trapezium has two parallel sides. $A=\frac12h(a+b)$. $a$ and $b$ are the parallel sides. $h$ is the perpendicular height.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: A trapezium has two parallel sides. $A=\frac12h(a+b)$. $a$ and $b$ are the parallel sides. $h$ is the perpendicular height. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.stage: Development: Example: parallel sides eight and ten centimetres
steps.content: Example: parallel sides eight and ten centimetres: Parallel sides are $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$; height is $7\text{ cm}$. $A=\frac12\times7(8+10)$. $A=\frac12\times7\times18$. $A=7\times9=63\text{ cm}^2$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: Parallel sides are $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$; height is $7\text{ cm}$. $A=\frac12\times7(8+10)$. $A=\frac12\times7\times18$. $A=7\times9=63\text{ cm}^2$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.stage: Development: Example: parallel sides seven and ten centimetres
steps.content: Example: parallel sides seven and ten centimetres: Parallel sides are $7\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$; height is $4\text{ cm}$. $A=\frac12\times4(7+10)$. $A=2\times17=34\text{ cm}^2$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: Parallel sides are $7\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$; height is $4\text{ cm}$. $A=\frac12\times4(7+10)$. $A=2\times17=34\text{ cm}^2$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.stage: Development: Example: finding the second parallel side
steps.content: Example: finding the second parallel side: Area is $60\text{ cm}^2$, height is $4\text{ cm}$ and one parallel side is $10\text{ cm}$. $\frac12\times4(a+10)=60$. $2(a+10)=60$. $2a+20=60$. $2a=40$. $a=20\text{ cm}$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: Area is $60\text{ cm}^2$, height is $4\text{ cm}$ and one parallel side is $10\text{ cm}$. $\frac12\times4(a+10)=60$. $2(a+10)=60$. $2a+20=60$. $2a=40$. $a=20\text{ cm}$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

source.quote: The area of a trapezium is 60cm 2

steps.content: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 7 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. A trapezium has area 60 square centimetres, height 4 cm and one parallel side 10 cm. Find the second parallel side. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 12 dm and 18 dm and height 8 dm. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 3 cm.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets these questions: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 7 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. A trapezium has area 60 square centimetres, height 4 cm and one parallel side 10 cm. Find the second parallel side. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 12 dm and 18 dm and height 8 dm. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 3 cm. The teacher checks each learner’s working, marks against these computed answers: ½ × 7 × (8 + 10) = 63 cm². ½ × 4 × (7 + 10) = 34 cm². ½ × 4 × (a + 10) = 60; a = 20 cm. ½ × 8 × (12 + 18) = 120 dm². ½ × 3 × (8 + 12) = 30 cm². and supports learners who confuse lengths, areas or units.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners solve the questions individually, show each calculation, compare marked answers, and correct any errors in substitution or units.

source.quote: Find the area of the trapezium below

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks learners to explain their solutions to these questions: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 7 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. A trapezium has area 60 square centimetres, height 4 cm and one parallel side 10 cm. Find the second parallel side. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 12 dm and 18 dm and height 8 dm. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 3 cm. The teacher checks the lesson objectives against the written work and assigns correction of the final exercise item.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain their calculation methods, state the correct units, and correct the final exercise item after receiving feedback.

assessment: Mark the written working for these questions: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 10 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Find the second parallel side. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 12 dm and 18 dm and height 8 dm. Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 3 cm. Check the stated measurements, operations, final answers and units against the answer key.
homework: Correct and fully work this exercise item: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 3 cm.
